# Whether the conversation state this build composes onto cursor's blob channel
# reaches the model — whether a second turn remembers the first — and what the
# server fetches of it.
#
# The recording W3's gate reads (.omc/plans/2026-09-07-cursor-history-blobs.md,
# W2; AC-13). Two live turns against api2.cursor.sh, both run by the user
# through `!` — no lane and no lead ran one, and nothing here was read out of
# auth.json. What the wire itself said is in the run's own log at `-v`; the
# line numbers below are that file's. The log was grepped for the three
# credential markers the lane charter names (a bearer prefix, a key prefix, a
# JWT header) before a line of this was written: zero hits over 7,015 lines.
#
# Recorded by: the shipped wire's own debug lines, no spike scaffolding this
#              time — history.rs's two lines at the end of `blobs` (:503,
#              :522: counts, then sorted id prefixes with sizes) and
#              request.rs's three in `kv_answer` (:595 get, :613 set, :631 a
#              set that replaced held bytes). Line numbers are 4a9ac1d's.
# Build:  ganja-code 0.1.0; ./target/release/ganja rebuilt from 4a9ac1d (W1,
#         "provider: carry the conversation on cursor's blob channel").
# Date:   2026-09-06, 18:16:37 - 18:17:29 UTC (2026-09-07 03:16 - 03:17 JST;
#         the log file is named by the local date).
# Log:    ~/.local/share/ganja/log/ganja.2026-09-07.log, 7,015 lines; the two
#         runs are :6810-:6921 and :6922-:7015, the last 206.
# Server: api2.cursor.sh. This client identified as cli-2026.01.09-231024f
#         (cursor.rs:138, sent as x-cursor-client-version at :557), the
#         constant cursor.rs has always sent.
# Model:  GANJA_MODEL unset on both runs, so the turn ran under cursor's
#         server-side `default` (Auto). Which model that resolved to is decided
#         server-side and is not observable from this client. The config's
#         `effort = "xhigh"` was dropped at adoption (:6816, :6930) because
#         `default` carries no effort ladder.
#
# What the wire carried that no request before 4a9ac1d did: on the second run,
# AgentRunRequest.conversation_state{root_prompt_messages_json = 6 ids,
# turns = 1 id}, every id the sha256 of bytes seeded into the Run's blob store
# before the stream opened, and AgentRunRequest.conversation_id on BOTH runs —
# derived from the first message's own id, so the same value on both, by
# construction (history.rs `derived`; the log never prints it).
#
# NO CONNECT ERROR OF ANY KIND WAS PRODUCED BY EITHER RUN. No `code`, no
# `message`, no EndStream error frame, no `Blob not found`, no
# `invalid_argument`, no ProviderEvent::Failed. The one line in the window
# that a case-insensitive grep for "failed" finds is :6851, a bridged `read`
# whose *tool* outcome was `failed` (file not found) — a tool result the model
# read, not a wire failure. The plan asks for every error code and message
# verbatim; the honest verbatim record is that there were none.
#
# This directory's rule holds here: no token, no tool-argument value and no
# reply text. What the user's terminal printed — the two replies — is
# described, never quoted; the lane charter under .omc/handoffs/ holds the
# stdout for whoever needs the exact bytes.

== probe 1 ==

== the runs ==
# One line per run: the command as the user ran it (GANJA_PROVIDER=cursor,
# nothing else set), the log window, and the run's turn — composition line
# to `step_completed (17)`.
R1  run -v "Remember the code word PELICAN-7. Reply with OK and nothing else."
                                     log :6810-:6921   turn :6819-:6912  (15.64 s)
R2  run -v --continue "What code word did I ask you to remember, and what is
    the current working directory? One line."
                                     log :6922-:7015   turn :6932-:7006  (9.22 s)

# Both runs ended by printing a reply and exiting; neither emitted a
# ProviderEvent::Failed. The wire logs no line for a clean EndStream and none
# for the run request's send, so "the turn completed" here means: a reply was
# printed, `step_completed (17)` was decoded (:6912, :7006), the process
# exited, and no failure was reported.

# R1's turn was not the no-call turn the plan's procedure assumed (A-M2: "turn
# 1 makes no call"). The model called three of ganja's tools through the
# declared roster, every one arriving as `mcp_args` and bridged (D552):
#
#   :6848  bridging an exec  exec=1 kind="mcp_args" tool="read"
#   :6851  answering a bridged exec  exec=1 tool="read"  outcome="failed"
#   :6853  bridging an exec  exec=2 kind="mcp_args" tool="glob"
#   :6859  answering a bridged exec  exec=2 tool="glob"  outcome="ran"
#   :6885  bridging an exec  exec=3 kind="mcp_args" tool="bash"
#   :6889  answering a bridged exec  exec=3 tool="bash"  outcome="refused"
#
# (the `read` answered file-not-found; the `glob` ran and matched nothing; the
# `bash` was auto-rejected, as a headless run without --auto rejects every
# dialog). The reply then printed the one word the prompt asked for. So R2's
# history carried an assistant entry with three `[Tool Call]` paragraphs and
# three result entries — two `[Tool Result (error)]`, one `[Tool Result]` —
# and the state below is larger than the plan's `entries = 3` by exactly
# those. See "incidental": this pre-measures W3's P3.
#
# R2's turn made one call, `bash` (:6961, exec=1, kind="mcp_args"), refused
# the same way (:6967 outcome="refused"), and answered anyway.

== P1 — does the composed history reach the model ==
VERDICT: YES

The second reply named the code word the first prompt asked the model to
remember, in one line beside the working directory. Nothing in R2's own
prompt carries the word; the only channel it could have reached the model by
is the state below.

R2's composition, :6932-:6933:

  :6932  composed the conversation state provider="cursor" entries=6 turns=1
         blobs=12 bytes=171566 clamped_calls=0 action="user"
  :6933  the composed blob ids provider="cursor" ids=[
           "08dfcb1a9e5054ba=86",   "24551d6ffef6a9a4=633",  "449d69fc21ec4914=173",
           "50b657d2779825dc=549",  "5fab41de977ff5dd=198",  "88a3603a48ff45bc=150",
           "9b2c0716baa430d1=136",  "a01d5bda822aaef7=32",   "c5ab3958edfbbe51=169304",
           "e0e4ac3d0f3ef169=82",   "f31f7f6c3ce521d5=118",  "fdebda7208d1cfd0=105" ]

entries=6 is the system head, R1's user message, R1's assistant entry (its
text and three `[Tool Call]` paragraphs), and three result entries; turns=1
is R1's one turn; blobs=12 is 6 root JSON entries + 1 UserMessage + 4
ConversationSteps + 1 ConversationTurn, and the twelve sizes sum to 171,566.

The server's gets, :6935-:6941 — seven, all within 48 µs of one another
(18:17:21.665657Z - .665705Z: one batch), 0.98 s after the composition line,
before any set, and every one answered found:

  :6935  answering the server's kv get blob="449d69fc21ec4914" found=173
  :6936  answering the server's kv get blob="9b2c0716baa430d1" found=136
  :6937  answering the server's kv get blob="c5ab3958edfbbe51" found=169304
  :6938  answering the server's kv get blob="f31f7f6c3ce521d5" found=118
  :6939  answering the server's kv get blob="24551d6ffef6a9a4" found=633
  :6940  answering the server's kv get blob="5fab41de977ff5dd" found=198
  :6941  answering the server's kv get blob="e0e4ac3d0f3ef169" found=82

(`found=<n>` is tracing's rendering of `Some(n)`; a miss would print the line
with no `found` field at all, and no such line exists in the window.)

Which composed ids were fetched and which were not. The log carries prefixes
and sizes only, but the twelve sizes decompose exactly against the shapes
history.rs builds (JSON frame 53 bytes for a `user` root entry, 58 for an
`assistant` one; every proto field here is number 1 or 2, so a 1-byte tag
plus a length):

  root[0]  c5ab3958edfbbe51  169304  system head, the one six-figure blob   FETCHED :6937
  root[1]  f31f7f6c3ce521d5     118  user: 53 + the 65-byte prompt           FETCHED :6938
  root[2]  24551d6ffef6a9a4     633  assistant text + 3 [Tool Call]s         FETCHED :6939
  root[3]  5fab41de977ff5dd     198  [Tool Result (error)] read: 53+144+1    FETCHED :6940
  root[4]  e0e4ac3d0f3ef169      82  [Tool Result] glob: 53+28+1 (the 28 is
                                     the marker, a newline, and glob.rs:96's
                                     own "No files found")                   FETCHED :6941
  root[5]  9b2c0716baa430d1     136  [Tool Result (error)] bash: 53+82+1
                                     (the 82: marker, newline, the 60-byte
                                     refusal sentence permission_text renders) FETCHED :6936
  turns[0] 449d69fc21ec4914     173  ConversationTurn: 1+2+(5 × (1+1+32)) —
                                     one user_message id and four step ids    FETCHED :6935
  turn.user_message
           fdebda7208d1cfd0     105  UserMessage: (1+1+65 text) +
                                     (1+1+36 derived message_id)             not fetched
  step[0]  50b657d2779825dc     549  the assistant text in proto framing
                                     (by elimination: 633 is the same text
                                     JSON-escaped, +58 frame)                not fetched
  step[1]  88a3603a48ff45bc     150  read result: 1+2+(1+2+144)              not fetched
  step[2]  a01d5bda822aaef7      32  glob result: 1+1+(1+1+28)               not fetched
  step[3]  08dfcb1a9e5054ba      86  bash result: 1+1+(1+1+82)               not fetched

Fetched: all six root entries (170,471 bytes) and the ConversationTurn
wrapper (173). Not fetched: the five blobs only that wrapper names — the
turn's user_message and its four steps (922 bytes). This is the reference's
own claim (`proxy.ts:744-750`: the server builds the prompt from
`root_prompt_messages_json`, not from `turns[]`) observed from the client
side, with one addition the reference does not state: the server does
dereference the turn *wrapper* — it just never follows the ids inside it. So
on this recording a divergence in the model's memory would trace to the root
and nowhere else, which is what history.rs's module doc predicted.

Fetch order was turns[0], root[5], root[0], root[1], root[2], root[3],
root[4] — the last root entry ahead of the first, in one batch. One sample;
nothing here says the order is stable.

Reading checklist (C-M5, C-M1'):

  * A get for an id this build never minted: NO. All seven gets name ids in
    the :6933 listing, and no get went unanswered-found. Five composed ids
    were never asked for; no asked-for id was uncomposed.

  * Either `message_id` echoed anywhere visible: NOT DETERMINABLE FROM THE
    LOG. This build prints neither id it minted — the history blob's derived
    one nor the action's random one (request.rs:230 `fresh_id`) — and a
    case-sensitive grep of the window for `message_id` and `conversation_id`
    returns nothing. The only server-minted ids the log shows are the tool
    call ids on the `bridging an exec` lines, shaped `call-<v4 uuid>-<n>`
    over `fc_<hex>_<n>`: R1's step-1 execs (:6848, :6853) share one uuid with
    indices -0/-1 and its step-2 exec (:6885) carries a different uuid with
    -2, so those are per-step mints of the server's own — a Run carries
    exactly one action message_id, and two distinct uuids appeared inside
    one Run. Whether one of them coincides with the id this client sent
    cannot be checked without the client printing it.

  * Anything in R2 attributable to `conversation_id`: NOTHING SEPARABLE.
    Both runs carried one — the same derived value — so the presence of the
    field is not a variable between them. R2 differs from R1 in exactly the
    ways the supplied state predicts (seven gets where R1 had none; a
    shorter turn with one call where R1 had three) and in one way it does
    not: R1's server set a 190,884-byte blob at :6826, 2.7 s in, and R2's
    server set nothing larger than 3,735 bytes (:7004) in the whole run.
    That could be the server declining to write its own head because the
    client supplied a root, or the server recognizing a conversation_id it
    had seen 43 s earlier; one recording cannot tell those apart.

== P1b — does the working directory arrive (smoke, not a discriminator) ==
VERDICT: YES — and it proves only "at least one channel"

The reply's second half was the checkout's absolute path, which is what the
system prompt's `<env>` block carries. It did not come from a tool: the one
thing the model tried, `bash` (:6961), was refused (:6967), and the reply
was printed anyway.

Why this settles nothing about which channel: the plan's own sentence — "Both
channels carry the *same* string (`cloud_rule` is `request.system` at
`request.rs:257`; the head is the same `request.system`), so a correct
directory proves only that the system prompt reached the model by **at least
one** channel; it cannot say which, and doubling is not observable from this
side at all." At 4a9ac1d that line is request.rs:301, not :257 — the plan's
number predates W1's edits to the file. On R1 there was no head (entries=0,
:6819: "the system head appears only beside history"), so R1's directory
could only have come from `cloud_rule`; on R2 both channels carried it.

== P2 — every get found, no error frame, and what the fetch cost ==
VERDICT: YES

Every get for a composed id was found (the seven lines above). No `Blob not
found`, no `invalid_argument`, no EndStream error, no Failed event in either
run's window; `a server set replaced bytes this run already held` (the :631
line, which would name a differing re-set of a held id) appears zero times
in the window and zero times in the whole 7,015-line log.

Gets before the first model output, and the wall time to it. This build logs
no line for a text delta (decode.rs:346-347 emits the event silently; only
thinking deltas are logged, :357) and none for the run request's send, so the
two ends measurable here are the composition line — logged inside
`run_message`'s assembly, immediately before the send — and the first
`thinking delta`. The number is therefore an upper bound on send-to-first-
thinking, and the first *text* delta is later by an amount the log does not
show.

  R2  composition :6932 18:17:20.681416Z
      gets        :6935-:6941 at +0.984 s (7, all found, 170,644 bytes served)
      sets        :6945-:6947 at +1.964 s (3: 2262, 260, 225)
      first thinking delta :6948 18:17:24.259983Z    = +3.579 s
      gets before that delta: 7   sets before it: 3

  R1  composition :6819 18:16:37.810929Z
      gets        none
      sets        :6825 at +2.012 s (2262), :6826-:6828 at +2.663 s
                  (190884, 90, 196)
      first thinking delta :6829 18:16:45.071990Z    = +7.261 s
      gets before that delta: 0   sets before it: 4

Read carefully: the run that fetched 171 KB of state reached its first
thinking 3.7 s *sooner* than the run that fetched nothing. One sample per
arm, one model, one afternoon — this is not a measurement of the fetch's
cost, and the ADR's expiry clause should read it as "the seven gets and
their 170 KB did not push TTFT past the empty-state run's own", not as a
saving. What the two numbers do bound: the batch of seven gets was issued
and answered within one second of the request going out, and the model was
producing 1.6 s after the server's first set.

== P4-pre — the checkpoint arm ==
VERDICT: ARRIVES, on both runs: 12 times, n from 558 to 7465

`unmodelled server-message fields provider="cursor" fields=[(3, n)]`:

  R1  :6862 (3, 7465)  :6871 (3, 558)   :6890 (3, 2578)  :6897 (3, 626)
      :6909 (3, 1882)  :6911 (3, 660)   :6913 (3, 660)                   7 arrivals
  R2  :6968 (3, 3269)  :6975 (3, 683)   :7003 (3, 4499)  :7005 (3, 717)
      :7007 (3, 717)                                                    5 arrivals

Placement, the same on both runs: one arrives after each tool_call_completed
or kv-set burst, and the run's last two are a pair of identical size that
brackets `step_completed (17)` (:6912 between the two 660s; :7006 between the
two 717s). The largest, 7465 at :6862, followed R1's first two bridged execs.
Only the size is seen; the arm is not decoded.

== what this cannot measure ==

1. One seat, one account, one model (`default`/Auto), one client version,
   one afternoon, one turn of history. Nothing here says what a named model,
   a different tier, or a later server does — nor what a *longer* history
   does: R2 named one turn (12 blobs); a session of ten turns, or one whose
   history has been re-rooted by compaction, is unmeasured.

2. Head doubling is not observable from this side. R2 carried
   `request.system` twice — as root[0] and as `cloud_rule` — and a model
   that reads both, either, or one twice leaves the same trace here. The
   P1b section says why the directory cannot discriminate.

3. Server-side use of `conversation_id` is not observable. Both runs sent
   the same derived value; nothing came back that names it, and the one
   behavioural difference not explained by the supplied state (the 190 KB
   set on R1 only) has two candidate causes this recording cannot separate.

4. Nothing about a bridged (paused) Run's *history* — a step that resumes
   from `Action::Resume` with the assistant's message last. Every request
   here was `action="user"`; the Resume arm was never sent. That is probe
   2's.

5. Whether the five unfetched blobs are *never* read, or merely were not
   read on this turn. One recording of one server: the turn's user_message
   and steps were not dereferenced here, which matches the reference's
   claim, and does not prove the server has no path that would.

6. The `[Tool Call]` input clamp: `clamped_calls=0` on every composition,
   because no call's input reached 8 KiB. The elision text and the count are
   unit-tested, not live-measured.

7. First-*text*-delta timing, the run request's send instant, and the clean
   EndStream: none has a log line in this build, so every timing above is
   composition-to-first-thinking and "the turn completed" is inferred from
   the printed reply, the decoded step_completed and the clean exit.

8. What the checkpoint arm (3, n) carries: only its byte count reaches the
   log, and whether it is a checkpoint at all is the plan's naming, not a
   decoded fact.

== incidental, and worth knowing before W3 ==

* `[Tool Call]` and `[Tool Result …]` text was sent and accepted a wave
  early. Because R1's model called three tools, R2's request was the first
  this build has ever sent carrying an assistant root entry with `[Tool
  Call]` paragraphs (root[2], 633 bytes) and both result flavours (root[3]
  and root[5] as `(error)`, root[4] plain) — and the reply was correct. W3's
  P3 was to be the first measurement of that shape; it is pre-measured here
  for the un-paused case. The plan's A-M2 attribution premise ("It carries
  no `[Tool Call]` text") did not hold on this recording; since P1 passed,
  nothing needed attributing.

* Every exec on both runs arrived as `mcp_args` — the model reached ganja's
  `read`, `glob` and `bash` by the names the roster declared, never through
  a native kind redirected (D552's second door). Each hold was short: 106 ms
  (:6850→:6851), 66 ms (:6858→:6859), 110 ms (:6888→:6889), 70 ms
  (:6966→:6967).

* `ganja run` still constructs the cursor wire twice per invocation (the
  reference probe's first incidental). Here it shows as a second
  composition with `entries=0` at :6918 and :7012, at process teardown
  after step_completed — the title/summary one-shot — followed by no get
  and no set: composed and logged, never sent.

* The first kv set of each run is the same blob at the same size:
  `a3b587832706c9c6` size=2262 at :6825 and :6945. The server's set ids are
  deterministic across processes for at least that one blob.

* R1's server set a 190,884-byte blob (:6826) before its first delta — the
  reference probe saw one of that order on its R5 (185,582 bytes); R2's
  server never set anything above 3,735 bytes. Two candidate causes, above;
  one recording.

* kv sets in the window: 24 on R1, 15 on R2, 39 in all. (148 is the whole
  day's log, every session since 00:00 local.)

* The MCP servers a session dials at startup (context7 at :6942, the gemini
  plugin at :6944) connected *after* the seven gets had been answered
  (:6935-:6941). They did not gate the run request.

* Beside the `partial_tool_call (7)`, `tool_call_started (2)` and
  `tool_call_completed (3)` arms this build skips, every one of those lines
  also names an unmodelled `field 25` on the update (:6844, :6846, :6847,
  :6852, :6860, …). Unchanged from before W1; noted because a reader of
  this log will see it beside every tool call.

# Recorded at W3, after the recovery (D553, second half) lands: a bridged
# Run paused on a tool call, its held Run gone, resumed from the composed
# state with `Action::Resume`. Not yet run.
